title: Bell nonlocality from finitely many copies of every entangled state
formal: For every entangled finite-dimensional bipartite state \(\rho\), do finitely many copies \(\rho ^{\otimes}k\) and local filters suffice to produce correlations violating a Bell inequality, without an auxiliary entangled state?
definitions: A state is a positive semidefinite trace-one operator on \(H_{A}\otimes H_{B}\). It is entangled when it is not a convex combination of product states. Local filters are trace-nonincreasing completely positive maps \(F_{A},F_{B}\) applied to the respective k-fold systems before measurement questions are selected; the joint success probability must be positive. Normalize the successful filtered state. Each party then chooses a local measurement from a finite set of positive-operator-valued measurements. The resulting conditional distribution p(a,b|x,y) is Bell-nonlocal when it has no representation \(\sum_{\lambda} q_{\lambda} p_{A}(a|x,\lambda )p_{B}(b|y,\lambda )\), with nonnegative \(q_{\lambda}\) summing to one. Such a representation is precisely a local hidden-variable model for finite questions and answers. Local ancillary states and shared randomness are allowed, but no additional shared entangled state is supplied.

context_blocks.text: Entanglement and observable Bell nonlocality are related but distinct resources. This question asks whether repeated access to the same entanglement always reveals nonlocal behavior after local preprocessing.

Liang, Masanes and Rosset prove an activation result using a suitable auxiliary state. That resource is stronger than additional copies of the given state and is expressly excluded here. Direct one-copy Bell tests also do not settle the finite-copy filtered target.

why: Determine whether every bipartite entangled state has an intrinsic finite-copy nonlocal manifestation.
answer_criterion: Prove the stated proposition or its logical negation, with the specified quantifiers, model and guarantees. A conditional theorem settles only that conditional claim. Benchmark acceptance requires a complete proof-assistant-checked proof of the full target.
